extracted.intended_audience: humor writers submitting short pieces to McSweeney's Internet Tendency
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for crafting and submitting short, literary/conceptual humor pieces to McSweeney's Internet Tendency, covering title, length, acceptable formats, voice, and premise requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces should have titles that quickly lure readers in. The editor will be drawn to submissions with funny, eye-catching titles that cleverly reveal the premises of pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should both attract attention and reveal or imply the piece's premise; prefer titles that make the conceit obvious and enticing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces under 1,000 words. Absolute maximum 1,200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for concise short pieces; do not exceed 1,200 words and preferably stay below 1,000 to meet editorial expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable Formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists; Open letters to people who are unlikely to respond; Monologues; Food reviews; Short satire / conceptual humor pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the formats McSweeney's favors — lean into conceptual or character-driven forms rather than conventional personal essays or straight news-parody.

rubrics_metrics.name: What NOT to Submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of goofy email names from spam or funny texts from drunk friends; Personal essays; Submissions formatted like news articles ("there is a better website that already does this" — i.e., The Onion); "Fake news" format pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid derivative or format-driven pieces that mimic other outlets (especially The Onion) or that rely on aggregating found funny texts; editorial preference is for original, constructed conceits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: McSweeney's has a specific voice different from other places. Read the site regularly to understand it. Tends toward: literary, conceptual, character-driven, often academic-tinged absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the site's tone: prioritize literary phrasing, conceptual depth, character focus, and an often academic-tinged absurd sensibility rather than quick gag-jokes or listicle tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should reveal/imply the premise. The whole piece should sustain a single conceit. The conceit should be specific and tightly constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop one strong, specific conceit and sustain it through the piece without drifting; specificity and tight construction are valued over loose or sprawling premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Check — Single, clear conceit revealed by the title
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a single, clear conceit revealed by the title?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor looks for clarity of conceit and alignment between title and content; titles that hint at multiple competing premises weaken the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Check — Short length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces exceeding ~1,000 words are less likely to fit the section; the guidelines set an absolute cap at 1,200 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Check — Sustains conceit without padding
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it sustain the conceit without padding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler, extraneous detours, or padding that dilutes the conceit; every line should serve the central idea or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Check — Voice is literary/conceptual rather than gag-driven
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the voice literary/conceptual rather than gag-driven?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize sustained, character- or concept-driven humor; one-off punchline-driven pieces are less aligned with the site's editorial voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Check — Avoid being a personal essay or fake news
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it avoid being a personal essay or fake news?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions formatted as personal essays or as straight 'fake news' (news-parody in the style of The Onion) are discouraged; aim for original formats and conceptual humor.
